title: Diagnosing drought–flood vulnerability of rice systems across growth stages using Sentinel-1/2 and CHIRPS time series
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Compound and rapidly alternating drought and flood events pose a major challenge to rice production because crop impacts depend strongly on when hydroclimatic stress occurs and how crop condition evolves afterwards. Here, rice vulnerability is characterized by stage-specific exposure, sensitivity, and recovery. We developed a Stage-resolved Drought–flood Rice Vulnerability (SDRV) framework to diagnose vulnerability formation in stable single-season rice across the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River (MLYR), China, during 2020–2025. SDRV integrates CHIRPS precipitation and Sentinel-1/2 time-series within four regionally harmonized growth-stage windows: establishment to early tillering (S1), tillering to jointing (S2), booting/heading to grain filling (S3), and grain filling to maturity (S4). Stage-specific percentile mapping places the underlying hydroclimatic and canopy observations in a common 0–1 diagnostic space, after which the three components are integrated into stage-wise and annual vulnerability. Results show that annual vulnerability ranked as 2022 > 2025 > 2023 > 2020 > 2021 > 2024. Within the study period, drought-dominant and drought-involved pathways were associated with greater annual vulnerability than the flood-dominant pathway represented by 2020. Vulnerability amplification was concentrated mainly in S2–S3. In 2022, persistent drought-dominant stress intensified vulnerability toward S3, producing the highest annual mean vulnerability (0.599) and the largest high-vulnerability fraction (50.4%). In 2025, alternating drought and flood conditions generated a different pathway, with vulnerability concentrated in S2 and partially reduced in S3. Spatially, high vulnerability repeatedly formed a northern and central MLYR corridor, especially across Anhui, Jiangsu and adjoining parts of the middle Yangtze region. Province-level comparison with a yield-loss proxy further showed a positive external-consistency relationship for annual vulnerability after accounting for year effects. These results demonstrate that rice vulnerability under drought–flood stress develops through stage-dependent interactions among hydroclimatic forcing, canopy response, and subsequent recovery. SDRV therefore provides a process-oriented approach for identifying when and where vulnerability intensifies within the growing season.

title: Prior-Informed Spatially Adaptive Network (PISA-Net) for multi-parameter water quality retrieval in Poyang Lake using Sentinel-2 imagery
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Accurate retrieval of water-quality parameters from remote-sensing imagery is essential for monitoring large inland lakes, yet pronounced spatial heterogeneity and limited transferability across varying environmental conditions remain major challenges. This study proposes a Prior-Informed Spatially Adaptive Network (PISA-Net) for multi-parameter water-quality retrieval from Sentinel-2 imagery in Poyang Lake. PISA-Net integrates a CNN branch for nonlinear spectral–spatial feature learning with a knowledge-guided branch based on empirical optical descriptors and coordinate-derived geographic priors. A geographic soft-assignment mechanism constructs the spatial prior vector, which conditions CNN features through Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM), while a stop gradient consistency loss (SG-CL) promotes agreement between the two prediction pathways with controlled gradient propagation. Chl-a, TP, and CODMn were modeled independently and evaluated using 5-fold spatial-block cross-validation against six representative empirical, statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning baselines. PISA-Net achieved R 2 values of 0.6113, 0.5112, and 0.5054 for Chl-a, TP, and CODMn, respectively, consistently outperforming the strongest baseline, 2D-CNN, while reducing RMSE by approximately 29.6%, 21.4%, and 19.0%. An additional April 2018 cross-season experiment revealed substantial degradation under direct zero-shot transfer, whereas few-shot adaptation markedly reduced prediction errors, indicating useful cross-season adaptability after limited local calibration. Overall, PISA-Net provides a prior-informed spectral–spatial framework for water-quality retrieval under spatially heterogeneous conditions, while broader multi-season validation remains necessary to establish comprehensive seasonal generalizability.

title: Transforming Leaf-Off LiDAR to leaf-on canopy height models using deep learning
abstract: Accurate tree canopy metrics are essential for a wide range of ecological, environmental, and climate studies. Recent advances in airborne LiDAR sensing have greatly expanded access to high-resolution three-dimensional observations of tree canopy structure. However, many widely available airborne LiDAR datasets are acquired under leaf-off conditions to support terrain mapping, and our analysis across ecologically diverse sites shows that canopy height models (CHMs) derived from these data exhibit substantial, recurring discrepancies in canopy height and extent, with an overall tendency to underrepresent canopy structure relative to leaf-on conditions. These discrepancies limit the direct use of leaf-off CHMs in applications requiring canopy information representative of leaf-on conditions. To address this limitation, we introduce a deep learning framework for reconstructing leaf-on CHMs from existing leaf-off LiDAR-derived CHMs. To our knowledge, this is the first study to formulate the direct reconstruction of leaf-on CHMs from existing leaf-off LiDAR-derived CHMs as a supervised image-to-image learning task. The framework provides two complementary models: a Pix2Pix model that uses the leaf-off CHM alone and a U-Net model that additionally incorporates multispectral imagery. Our proposed models achieve robust canopy-height accuracy across four spatially independent test sites (R²: 0.85–0.92; Mean Absolute Error: 1.3–1.6 metres), substantially reducing the discrepancies observed in the leaf-off source CHMs. They also provide sharper delineation of canopy details and higher accuracy than recent optical-imagery-based approaches. To facilitate broader use, we developed an open-access web application that deploys the pre-trained models and supports on-demand leaf-on CHM generation for user-selected areas across the U.S. where suitable leaf-off LiDAR inputs are available. Overall, the framework provides a practical means to bridge the seasonal data gap in LiDAR acquisition and improve access to reliable canopy metrics representative of leaf-on conditions.

title: Efficient Time-Fractional Diffusion Network for Under-Display ToF Imaging and Beyond
CorrCLIPv2: Harnessing Unlabeled Images for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation
Cross-view guided remote sensing super-resolution via constrained residual refinement
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Existing RSISR reconstructs high-resolution imagery primarily from the degraded satellite observation, leaving missing fine-scale information underconstrained. We study whether geo-associated but geometrically misaligned ground imagery can provide useful auxiliary information for satellite super-resolution. We formulate Cross-View Guided Super-Resolution (CVG-SR) and propose Selective Residual Constrained Guidance (SRCG), which restricts ground-derived guidance to gated residual refinement around a satellite-conditioned reconstruction anchor. On VIGOR, matched ground guidance improves PSNR by 1.79 dB over the reconstruction anchor under realistic degradation and also outperforms fine-tuned satellite-only baselines. The advantage persists across higher magnification, different reconstruction anchors, and alternative guidance representations, while external-domain evaluations show that the effect remains observable under domain shift. The source code is available at https://github.com/zqluo-buaa/CVG-SR .

title: Passive microwave sea ice concentration biases in the Southern Hemisphere revealed by ICESat-2 linear ice fraction
abstract: Gridded sea ice concentration (SIC) data are fundamental for understanding long-term polar climate. Since 1978, daily SIC data have been derived from passive microwave (PM) satellite observations. As SIC is not directly observed, it is obtained through an algorithmic inversion of PM brightness temperatures. Differences between PM-SIC algorithms lead to uncertainty in SIC data. Here we examine differences between several PM-SIC products and focus primarily on two: the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC) Climate Data Record (CDR), which over our study period is derived from Special Sensor Microwave Imager/Sounder (SSMIS) data, and over the Southern Ocean is largely based on the Bootstrap (BT) PM-SIC algorithm, and the Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer 2 (AMSR2)-based NASATeam2 (NT2) product. On individual days, changes in integrated Antarctic sea ice area (SIA) can reach as high as 1.6 million km 2 in summer with relative differences up to 37% at the annual sea ice minimum. Using more than 1.8 million coincident observations of the ICESat-2 Linear Ice Fraction (LIF) from 2018 to 2024, we find BT-based PM-SIC data underestimate Antarctic SIC by a median of 0.2 in areas classified as the marginal ice zone (MIZ), corresponding to a median relative difference in SIC of 31%. This offset is seasonally, spatially, and parametrically consistent and yields differences in apparent MIZ extent as high as 4.4 million km 2 . The offset exceeds reported CDR uncertainties that average 0.07 and cannot be explained as a consequence of sensor differences. The parametric simplicity of the observed bias means these offsets can be parameterized as a function of BT SIC alone, which could lead to an improved SIC dataset for Antarctic studies.
